items.streamTitle: AI and peer feedback improved some feedback-literacy measures in a classroom study
items.streamSummary: Across 126 students in three intact classes, AI and peer feedback coincided with gains on some self-reported feedback-literacy dimensions; the teacher group showed no significant changes. Assignment was not randomized.
items.attribution: Yan and Meng — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Brain-computer interface review puts generalization ahead of peak accuracy
items.streamSummary: A new review argues that neural decoding must be tested across sessions, participants, tasks, hardware, and clinical conditions. High development scores alone do not establish durable clinical use.
items.attribution: Gu et al. — npj Biomedical Innovations (review)

items.streamTitle: Army AI supplier announced a $700 million enterprise contract ceiling
items.streamSummary: Striveworks said its enterprise agreement grew tenfold and would support more Army AI deployments. The headline figure is a ceiling, not funds spent or independently verified mission improvement.
items.attribution: Striveworks — company announcement, October 22

items.streamTitle: UNIDIR starts a 2026–27 AI security lexicon initiative
items.streamSummary: UNIDIR outlined a multidisciplinary effort to clarify AI security terminology for policymakers, including contested definitions. The October 23 event and plan are not evidence that agreement or adoption has occurred.
items.attribution: UNIDIR — official AI security lexicon event

items.streamTitle: Emergency managers ranked organizational context as central to AI adoption
items.streamSummary: Expert interviews and fuzzy DEMATEL analysis in China identified contextual and decision-process barriers to generative-AI adoption in crises. The findings are perceived relationships, not demonstrated effects.
items.attribution: Fei, Sun and Sun — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: More policy coverage tracked public participation, not necessarily favorable sentiment
items.streamSummary: Across 232 Chinese cities, talent-policy media attention had a nonlinear association with a combined response index, while sentiment alone did not show the same reversal. Causality was not established.
items.attribution: Li and Wang — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Review finds modest average gains from combining clinical text and structured records
items.streamSummary: A systematic review retained 57 of 641 studies and found a reported average 6.4% improvement for LLM-enabled multimodal prediction. Heterogeneous studies and deployment limits constrain the claim.
items.attribution: Kaster et al. — npj Digital Medicine (systematic review)

items.streamTitle: Phishing texts used urgency and action cues absent from a small legitimate sample
items.streamSummary: A linguistic comparison of 106 scam texts and 16 legitimate texts found frequent urgency, authority, and link-related cues in scams. It did not test whether new warnings reduce victimization.
items.attribution: Kawabata — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: China–Japan policy comparison highlights differing responses to AI plagiarism
items.streamSummary: A document-based comparison of Chinese policy and 359 Japanese universities identified institutional silence and a Japanese 'No Copy + Exceptions' approach. It did not test which policy prevents plagiarism.
items.attribution: Zhang and Chen — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Science-fiction seminars prompted reflection without measurable attitude change
items.streamSummary: A mixed-methods university study found useful qualitative reflection around science-fiction films, while exploratory pre/post climate and planetary-health measures did not change significantly.
items.attribution: Lüdorf, Ehlers and Nitsche — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: CauTrigger modeled candidate causes across biological regulatory layers
items.streamSummary: A Nature Methods study introduced hierarchical latent-variable causal modeling and reported improvements on synthetic and biological benchmarks. In-silico perturbations nominate testable triggers, not proven interventions.
items.attribution: Zhang et al. — Nature Methods

items.streamTitle: NATO plans a baseline-versus-AI test of targeting decision speed
items.streamSummary: At DiBaX26, NATO plans to test a targeting workflow across 11 allies using simulated and live targets, aiming for more than 50% less decision time. No achieved speed or accuracy results were published.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — official October 21 report

items.streamTitle: Major rule violations spread more readily than rule-following in an online experiment
items.streamSummary: A 750-person experiment found that observing serious rule-breaking increased violations, especially from political in-group members. Simulations suggested rare escalators could amplify noncompliance; real-world sanctions were absent.
items.attribution: Molleman et al. — Proceedings of the Royal Society B

items.streamTitle: Infant macaque attention differed by inherited social rank
items.streamSummary: Repeated eye tracking of 39 male infant rhesus macaques linked lower maternal social rank to more rapid eye movements during social viewing. This association is not proof of causation or a human finding.
items.attribution: Ford et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Familiar nature-loss language outperformed crisis framing
items.streamSummary: A randomized study of 7,338 U.S. adults found familiar extinction language elicited more concern than technical biodiversity terms; crisis labels offered little benefit. Actual behavior was not measured.
items.attribution: Bruine de Bruin et al. — npj Biodiversity

items.streamTitle: Higher subgroup AI accuracy sometimes reflected differing case mix
items.streamSummary: In two opioid-risk models, an apparently stronger AUC in Black patients narrowed after covariate matching. Subgroup accuracy gaps can reflect data distributions, not just algorithm quality.
items.attribution: Ladhania et al. — npj Health Systems

items.streamTitle: Driving scenes needing explanation drew somewhat longer descriptions
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 1,103 automated-driving annotations found explanation length moderately tracked perceived need (r=0.374), but prediction was weak. Driver comprehension and safety were not tested.
items.attribution: Kim et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: A simple interaction model predicted constrained-space choices
items.streamSummary: An online restroom-choice study used statistical-physics models to estimate site preferences and predict occupancy across layouts. Model fit does not establish individual motives or real-world generalization.
items.attribution: Franckart et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: EU Arctic strategy prioritizes monitoring and critical infrastructure
items.streamSummary: The European Commission's October 20 Arctic strategy adds maritime security, monitoring and infrastructure resilience priorities. Announced initiatives have not yet demonstrated operational results.
items.attribution: European Commission — official Arctic strategy announcement

items.streamTitle: AI language-learning satisfaction tracked perceived service support
items.streamSummary: Survey modeling of 978 AI language-learning users linked perceived service quality and support to satisfaction and reported performance. No causal improvement in tested language ability was established.
items.attribution: Lee, Li and Bi — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Brain-based cognition models predicted modest, variable shares of performance
items.streamSummary: A review found brain-based models often explained about 10–40% of cognitive variation, with lower estimates in cross-dataset tests. Imaging predictions are not direct measures of thought or causal mechanisms.
items.attribution: Christensen et al. — Communications Psychology (review)

items.streamTitle: Hong Kong cohort identified 35 predictors of later resilience
items.streamSummary: A longitudinal study of 26,210 people linked 35 earlier health, social and personal factors to later self-reported resilience. The design does not show that changing those factors causes resilience.
items.attribution: Ning et al. — Nature Mental Health

items.streamTitle: UNIDIR released new national security-and-defence AI strategy guidance
items.streamSummary: UNIDIR's 81-page October 19 guidelines distinguish strategy-development procedures from technical, legal and political requirements. The document offers governance guidance rather than evidence of policy effectiveness.
items.attribution: Afina, Mannsperger and Madziwa — UNIDIR guidelines

items.streamTitle: No tested input-noise method improved accuracy or reached 95% coverage
items.streamSummary: A groundwater forecasting experiment found accuracy–coverage trade-offs under simulated input noise. None improved baseline accuracy or achieved nominal interval coverage.
items.attribution: Shiri et al. — Scientific Reports
